Answer: C
Reason: Figure 1 shows diffuse bilateral alveolar opacities consistent with pulmonary edema (e.g., from salt water aspiration), which have completely cleared in Figure 2; this rapid resolution is characteristic of supportive care (oxygen/ventilation) allowing reabsorption of aspirated fluid, whereas pneumonia or cardiogenic edema typically resolve more slowly or require specific pharmacologic interventions not implied by the clean clearance.
